_comment: Policy lifecycle metadata (PAP). The Rego files are the RULES; this file is
their IDENTITY: who owns each policy, what it is for, what it applies to, and
which version is current. Rego alone is not a sufficient source of truth --
a reviewer cannot tell from a .rego file who owns it or whether it is live.
Bump `version` whenever a policy's rules change. The version is written onto
every decision the policy produces, so an audit row identifies exactly which
revision of which policy decided.
Phase 4.5 adds the `cp-*` policies. They live in a SEPARATE Rego package
(agentic_iam.control_plane) with its own combining algorithm, so control-plane
hardening cannot alter the semantics of resource authorization.
Phase 5 adds the human-approval policies. `human-approval` and `loan-approval`
live in the DATA plane (agentic_iam.authz) because they decide whether an
ACTION may proceed; `cp-humans` lives in the control plane because it decides
whether a PERSON may administer or approve. Human roles and agent capabilities
never meet in either.
Phase 5.5 adds `loan-amount`, which is where the amount-based authorization
boundary lives, and a `data` section. The data documents are policy
CONFIGURATION -- thresholds a risk committee changes -- kept apart from the
rules a security reviewer changes. The PAP pushes both, and reconciles both,
because a rule whose configuration is missing fails closed and an operator
needs to be able to see that before it bites.
Phase 6 adds `jit-issuance` and `jit-use`. They live in DIFFERENT packages on
purpose. `jit-use` is in the data plane (agentic_iam.authz) because deciding
whether a presented mandate covers an action IS the ordinary authorization
question. `jit-issuance` is in its own package (agentic_iam.jit) because
'may a mandate be issued, and with what bounds?' is a different question, and
evaluating it inside the data-plane combining algorithm would let an issuance
rule contribute a deny to an ordinary action that never asked for a mandate.
Phase 7 adds `a2a-transaction`. It lives in the DATA plane
(agentic_iam.authz) because 'may sender A cause action X on resource R?'
IS the ordinary authorization question -- unlike JIT issuance, which asks
a different one and earns its own package. It is ONE module on purpose:
splitting the payment bands out would have introduced a cross-module rule
name, and OPA compiles the whole set on every PUT, so an unloaded
dependency takes every gate down at once. Phase 7 introduces ZERO new
cross-module names, and `decision.rego` and `security/sensitive.rego` are
untouched.

policies.description: Combining algorithm (deny-overrides, default-deny) and shared credential helpers.
policies.purpose: Guarantee that the absence of a matching policy denies rather than permits.

policies.description: Permit reading credit_records with a valid credit_analysis credential for loan_assessment; deny a mismatched purpose.
policies.purpose: Allow legitimate credit analysis during a loan assessment.

policies.description: Deny any resource the subject's valid credentials do not name in allowedResources.
policies.purpose: Ensure a valid credential confers scoped access, never unlimited access.

policies.description: Deny on missing, expired, revoked or otherwise invalid credentials, on an unresolvable subject, and (v2, added in Phase 6) on a registered subject whose identity is not ACTIVE.
policies.purpose: Translate the Phase 2 verifier's verdict into an authorization outcome.

policies.description: Escalate sensitive actions to HUMAN_APPROVAL_REQUIRED while they are UNAPPROVED. v2 (Phase 5) added the approval condition; v3 (Phase 5.5) stands aside for the two amount bands loan-amount owns, so a small loan is not escalated and a large one is escalated to two people.
policies.purpose: Mark actions that must not proceed on agent authority alone.

policies.description: Control-plane combining algorithm (deny-overrides, default-deny) and shared principal helpers.
policies.purpose: Guarantee that an unrecognised control-plane request denies rather than proceeds.

policies.description: An agent may heartbeat, deregister and ask the PDP about ITSELF, and nothing else. Denies acting for another agent and denies any administrative operation.
policies.purpose: Close S-4: bind ANS liveness to proof of control of the registered identity.

policies.description: Map each administrative control-plane operation to the single role it requires. Least privilege: the identity administrator cannot activate policy.
policies.purpose: Close S-5 and S-6: policy administration and identity signing require an authorized administrator.

policies.description: Turn the approval service's verdict into an authorization outcome: bound, valid and signed by ENOUGH DISTINCT HUMANS contributes to ALLOW; expired/consumed/rejected/tampered/forged, too few approvers, a repeated approver, and a retired, unknown or revoked signing key each deny by name.
policies.purpose: Ensure a human decision is re-evaluated by policy rather than becoming an ALLOW on its own.

policies.description: Permit approve_loan on loan_applications only with BOTH a valid scoped capability credential AND a valid bound human approval.
policies.purpose: Make human approval an additional requirement, never a substitute for the agent's own authority.

policies.description: Human control-plane authority: IAM_ADMIN administers identity (S-7), LOAN_OFFICER approves loan decisions, AUDITOR reads. No role is a superset of another, and an agent may not approve.
policies.purpose: Close S-7 and authorize approvals, keeping human roles and agent capabilities in separate trust domains.
policies.scope: principal.type=human, plus the agent self-approval refusal

policies.description: Amount-based loan authorization: below the autonomous limit the agent's own credential decides; up to the single-approver limit one LOAN_OFFICER approves; above it two distinct humans must. Denies when the thresholds are not loaded or the amount cannot be established.
policies.purpose: Close the Phase 5 gap in which a loan officer could approve any amount, and put the risk boundary in policy rather than in application code.

policies.description: Decide whether a JIT mandate may be issued for an already-permitted action, and with what TTL and use ceilings. Refuses an action that is not on the eligibility allow-list, one that policy escalates to a human, and any request over the configured bounds.
policies.purpose: Ensure a mandate can only ever be issued for something the agent could do at that instant, and never as a substitute for human approval.

policies.description: Turn the JIT service's verdict about a presented mandate into an authorization outcome: expired, revoked, exhausted, forged, tampered, out of scope, over a ceiling, or resting on credentials that have since been revoked each deny by name.
policies.purpose: Make a mandate an INPUT to authorization that every ordinary rule still runs alongside -- never a permission that replaces them.
policies.scope: any request presenting a JIT grant

policies.description: Permit READING a loan application with a valid credit_analysis credential scoped to loan_applications for loan_assessment. Grants no authority over approve_loan.
policies.purpose: Give the Phase 6 mandate ceiling (max_amount_inr) a live path: an amount-bearing action that is not an approval action, so the financial boundary is exercised without touching dual control.

policies.description: Agent-to-agent transaction authorization: turn the A2A service's verdict about a signed envelope into an authorization outcome, and decide a payment by amount band. Below the autonomous limit the sender's own credential decides; up to the single-approver limit one PAYMENT_OFFICER approves; above it TWO distinct humans must. Denies on a forged, tampered, stale, replayed or misaddressed envelope, on an ineligible action, and when the signed amount disagrees with the amount the server holds.
policies.purpose: Ensure a valid signature is an INPUT to authorization and never a substitute for one, and that a signed amount is never trusted merely because it is signed.
policies.scope: any request carrying an A2A transaction envelope

data.description: Loan approval thresholds, the approver role, and the maker-checker switch. Read by loan/amount.rego and control_plane/humans.rego.
data.purpose: Keep the NUMBERS that define risk appetite separate from the RULES that define what a number means.
data.fails_closed: loan/amount.rego denies with LOAN_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED when this document is not loaded. An absent threshold is never 'no limit'.

data.description: JIT bounds: maximum TTL, maximum uses, which actions may be mandated at all, and the amount ceiling a mandate may carry.
data.purpose: Keep the NUMBERS that bound a temporary mandate separate from the RULES that define what a bound means.
data.fails_closed: jit/issuance.rego denies with JIT_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED when this document is not loaded. An absent maximum TTL is never 'unlimited'.

data.description: A2A payment bands, the approver role, and which actions may be instructed agent-to-agent at all. Read by a2a/transaction.rego.
data.purpose: Keep the NUMBERS that define payment risk appetite separate from the RULES that define what a number means.
data.fails_closed: a2a/transaction.rego denies with A2A_POLICY_UNCONFIGURED when this document is not loaded. An absent threshold is never 'no limit'.
